description: Developer-annotated pilot: 12 fact-check cases covering conflicts, compatibility, missing and ambiguous scenarios. Each entry has expected status and the author's honest notes on actual CLI output.

cases.scenario: Same FY, same currency, different amounts
cases.text:
Parks FY27: $8 million
Parks FY27: $4 million
cases.notes: Straightforward. Groups under 'parks fy27' with unit=$. Normalized values 8e6 vs 4e6 produce conflict status. Exit 1.

cases.scenario: Table with same agency and year heading, different figures
cases.text:
| Agency | FY27 budget |
|---|---|
| Parks | $4 million |
| Parks | $8 million |
cases.notes: Table coordinates retained correctly. Label is 'parks fy27 budget'. Row 3 has $4M, row 4 has $8M. Conflict detected.

cases.scenario: Decimal vs integer representation of same value
cases.notes: Decimal 72e5 normalised identically to comma-grouped integer 72e5. Correctly compatible. No false positive.
Trivially compatible identical mentions. £ unit handled correctly.

cases.scenario: Same amount, different syntactic forms (comma grouping)
cases.notes: Comma grouping stripped. Both normalise to 8e6. Compatible.
Percentage unit (%) handled. Identical normalised values are compatible.

cases.scenario: Different attribute words ('shortfall' vs 'deficit'), same FY and value
cases.text:
FY27 shortfall: $8 million
FY27 deficit: $8 million
cases.notes: Labels are 'fy27 shortfall' and 'fy27 deficit' — two separate groups, both unresolved. The anchor 'FY27' does not merge across different attribute words. Conservative but misses a compatibility relationship a human would see.
Single mention, one group, status unresolved. Correctly refuses to judge.

cases.scenario: Same label, different currencies ($ vs £), same magnitude
cases.text:
FY27 grant: $8 million
FY27 grant: £8 million
cases.notes: Two groups both labelled 'fy27 grant' — one unit=$, one unit=£. Each has one mention, both unresolved. The tool partitions by unit so they are never compared. No unit-mismatch warning is emitted. A human reviewer would need to notice the split groups.

cases.scenario: Approximate qualifier (~) — assumed blocked, actually handled
cases.notes: SURPRISE: The tilde does NOT block extraction. The checker parses '~$8 million' with unit 'approximate $' and normalised value '8e6'. Two identical approximate values are compatible. This is better than the author expected. Risk: exact $8M and ~$8M form different units and are never compared.

cases.scenario: Same label, percentage vs raw count — different semantics
cases.notes: Two groups both labelled 'support'. One unit=%, one unit=count. Both unresolved. Tool partitions by unit so they are never compared. A human would ask: is 50 an absolute count or a percentage?

cases.scenario: Two programmes, same FY and same dollar amount, different names
cases.text:
FY27 food aid: $5 million
FY27 fuel aid: $5 million
cases.notes: Labels 'fy27 food aid' and 'fy27 fuel aid' are separate groups. Both contain one mention, both unresolved. Same $5 million value but tool cannot confirm they refer to different programmes. At two lines this works; on one line with '. ' separator the tool extracts 0 facts.
